The port is complete and verified. Final state of the delivery:

## `/work/rust/` — the Rust port

```
Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, src/{main,lib,httpd,handlers,repo,model,de,json,security,db,javaser,errorpage}.rs, tests/api.rs
```
No `target/`, no Java anywhere. `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` (19 unit tests + a full integration scenario against `DATABASE_URL`) pass, and the binary answers on `/rest/...` within a second of starting with `DATABASE_URL` and `PORT`.

## How it was verified

I ran the original Java app (jetty, its own recreated demo database) side by side with the Rust service on an identically-loaded `schema.sql` database and built a 220-step differential harness that fired every request at **both** services and compared **status codes, parsed JSON bodies, and the full contents of 29 database tables after every single step**. Result: **220 steps, 3 differences** — all three being the raw Java stack trace embedded inside the 500 page for `output:only` on `/rest/layerdatasources` (status, headers, page structure and exception message match; the JVM frames have no Rust counterpart).

Along the way the harness caught and the port now reproduces every quirk of the original, e.g.:

- **Auth**: bcrypt `$2a/$2y/$2b` with Spring's regex, inactive/no-roles users → 401, group roles aggregated, `ROLE_ADMIN > ROLE_USER` hierarchy, Jetty's exact 401/403 pages (rendered only for GET/HEAD/PUT-family differences), `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="SHOGun Realm"`.
- **Permissions**: PostFilter on lists and the relation endpoints, PostAuthorize/PreAuthorize on single entities, per-entity evaluator rules, user/group permission collections, ADMIN grant — including the self-invocation quirk that `/users/{id}/userGroups` checks only its members, not the user itself.
- **Status mapping**: denied POST → 400, denied PUT/DELETE/GET → 404, type mismatch → 400, PATCH → 405 with Spring's exact Allow headers and status text.
- **JSON**: Jackson key order, Java `Double.toString` (`2.002637639E7`), write-only passwords, id-only `userGroups`, the abstract `LayerDataSource` refusal, unknown-field rejection, and the fact that deserialized entity sets collapse to the first element (their `created` field is `@JsonIgnore`, so they are all `equals()`).
- **Writes**: `hibernate_sequences` allocation (`next_val+1`, surviving failed transactions, row auto-created as 1 on a missing row), join-table replacement/dereference, FK/unique-violation rollbacks, `@Cascade(SAVE_UPDATE)` wipe semantics with `NonUniqueObjectException` on session ids, `LayerService.delete`'s `maps_layers` renumbering, WMTS tile-grid cascade delete, and the OpenSessionInView quirk where a failed PUT still flushes the fields deserialized before the error.
- **XYZ resolutions**: byte-exact Java serialization of `java.awt.geom.Point2D$Double` (the field is `List<Point2D.Double>` because of a wildcard import), read back and re-written exactly as the original does.

//! PostgreSQL access: connection pool and the Hibernate table-generator
//! id allocation against `hibernate_sequences` (segment `default`).

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use tokio_postgres::Client;
use tokio_postgres::NoTls;

pub struct Pool {
    url: String,
    inner: Arc<PoolInner>,
}

struct PoolInner {
    clients: Mutex<Vec<Client>>,
}

impl Clone for Pool {
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        Pool { url: self.url.clone(), inner: self.inner.clone() }
    }
}

impl Pool {
    pub fn new(url: &str) -> Pool {
        Pool { url: url.to_string(), inner: Arc::new(PoolInner { clients: Mutex::new(Vec::new()) }) }
    }

    pub async fn connect_raw(url: &str) -> Result<Client, tokio_postgres::Error> {
        let (client, connection) = tokio_postgres::connect(url, NoTls).await?;
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            // Drive the connection to completion; when it ends the client is dead.
            let _ = connection.await;
        });
        Ok(client)
    }

    /// Take a client from the pool, creating a new one when needed.
    pub async fn get(&self) -> Result<PooledClient, tokio_postgres::Error> {
        if let Some(c) = self.inner.clients.lock().unwrap().pop() {
            return Ok(PooledClient { client: Some(c), pool: self.inner.clone() });
        }
        let c = Pool::connect_raw(&self.url).await?;
        Ok(PooledClient { client: Some(c), pool: self.inner.clone() })
    }

    pub async fn connect_with_retry(
        url: &str,
        tries: u32,
        delay_ms: u64,
    ) -> Result<Client, tokio_postgres::Error> {
        let mut last_err = None;
        for i in 0..tries {
            match Pool::connect_raw(url).await {
                Ok(c) => return Ok(c),
                Err(e) => {
                    last_err = Some(e);
                    if i + 1 < tries {
                        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay_ms)).await;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Err(last_err.expect("at least one try"))
    }
}

/// A checked-out client. Returned to the pool on drop; a broken
/// connection is discarded instead.
pub struct PooledClient {
    client: Option<Client>,
    pool: Arc<PoolInner>,
}

impl std::ops::Deref for PooledClient {
    type Target = Client;
    fn deref(&self) -> &Client {
        self.client.as_ref().expect("client present")
    }
}

impl std::ops::DerefMut for PooledClient {
    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Client {
        self.client.as_mut().expect("client present")
    }
}

impl Drop for PooledClient {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(c) = self.client.take() {
            if !c.is_closed() {
                self.pool.clients.lock().unwrap().push(c);
            }
        }
    }
}

impl PooledClient {
    /// Explicitly hand a healthy client back (equivalent to dropping it).
    pub async fn recycle(self) {}
}

/// Error while allocating an id. `Null` means the `hibernate_sequences` row
/// existed but `next_val` was NULL (the original fails with an NPE there).
pub enum IdErr {
    Db(tokio_postgres::Error),
    Null,
}

impl From<tokio_postgres::Error> for IdErr {
    fn from(e: tokio_postgres::Error) -> Self {
        IdErr::Db(e)
    }
}

/// Allocate a new id exactly the way Hibernate's enhanced `TableGenerator`
/// does with the `hibernate_sequences` table (segment value `default`):
///
/// * row present: `new id = next_val + 1`, then `next_val = new id`
/// * row missing: insert the row with `next_val = 1` and use id 1
///
/// The allocation commits independently of the surrounding write
/// transaction, just like the original (a failed create still advances
/// the sequence).
pub async fn allocate_id(client: &Client) -> Result<i32, IdErr> {
    let rows = client
        .query(
            "UPDATE hibernate_sequences SET next_val = next_val + 1 \
             WHERE sequence_name = 'default' RETURNING next_val",
            &[],
        )
        .await?;
    if let Some(row) = rows.first() {
        let v: Option<i64> = row.get(0);
        let next: i64 = v.ok_or(IdErr::Null)?;
        return Ok(next as i32);
    }
    // No row yet: Hibernate inserts one and allocates the initial value (1).
    let inserted = client
        .execute(
            "INSERT INTO hibernate_sequences (sequence_name, next_val) VALUES ('default', 1) \
             ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
            &[],
        )
        .await?;
    if inserted == 0 {
        // Someone else created the row concurrently: retry the update path.
        for _ in 0..10 {
            let rows = client
                .query(
                    "UPDATE hibernate_sequences SET next_val = next_val + 1 \
                     WHERE sequence_name = 'default' RETURNING next_val",
                    &[],
                )
                .await?;
            if let Some(row) = rows.first() {
                let next: Option<i64> = row.get(0);
                return Ok(next.ok_or(IdErr::Null)? as i32);
            }
            tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
        }
        return Err(IdErr::Null);
    }
    Ok(1)
}

//! Jackson-compatible JSON deserialization of the entity model.
//!
//! Mirrors `ObjectMapper.readValue` for POST bodies and
//! `objectMapper.readerForUpdating(entity).readValue(json)` for PUT bodies:
//! the passed entity is pre-populated (with loaded values or with the Java
//! constructor defaults) and only keys present in the JSON object are
//! applied. Unknown keys are rejected exactly like Jackson's default
//! `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES`; `@JsonIgnore` properties are silently
//! skipped; the abstract `LayerDataSource` cannot be built from JSON at all.

use crate::json::JVal;
use crate::model::*;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct DeErr;

const IGNORED: [&str; 4] = ["created", "modified", "userPermissions", "groupPermissions"];

fn obj<'a>(v: &'a JVal) -> Result<&'a Vec<(String, JVal)>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Obj(o) => Ok(o),
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

/// Jackson `String` deserialization: strings pass through, scalars coerce.
fn jstr(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<String>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Str(s) => Ok(Some(s.clone())),
        JVal::Int(i) => Ok(Some(i.to_string())),
        JVal::Float(f) => Ok(Some(crate::json::java_double(*f))),
        JVal::Bool(b) => Ok(Some(if *b { "true".into() } else { "false".into() })),
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

fn jdouble(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<f64>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Int(i) => Ok(Some(*i as f64)),
        JVal::Float(f) => Ok(Some(*f)),
        JVal::Str(s) => s.parse::<f64>().map(Some).map_err(|_| DeErr),
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

/// Jackson `Integer` deserialization (wrapper type; JSON null becomes None).
fn jint(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<i32>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Int(i) => {
            if *i >= i32::MIN as i64 && *i <= i32::MAX as i64 {
                Ok(Some(*i as i32))
            } else {
                Err(DeErr)
            }
        }
        JVal::Float(f) => {
            // Jackson coerces non-integral numbers by truncation
            // (4.9 -> 4); only out-of-range values fail
            if *f >= i32::MIN as f64 && *f <= i32::MAX as f64 {
                Ok(Some(*f as i32))
            } else {
                Err(DeErr)
            }
        }
        JVal::Str(s) => s.trim().parse::<i32>().map(Some).map_err(|_| DeErr),
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

/// Jackson primitive `int` deserialization (JSON null becomes 0).
fn jint_prim(v: &JVal) -> Result<i32, DeErr> {
    Ok(jint(v).unwrap_or(None).unwrap_or(0))
}

fn jbool(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<bool>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Bool(b) => Ok(Some(*b)),
        JVal::Str(s) => match s.as_str() {
            "true" => Ok(Some(true)),
            "false" => Ok(Some(false)),
            _ => Err(DeErr),
        },
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

/// joda-time `LocalDate` (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, calendar-validated).
fn jdate(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<String>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Str(s) => {
            if valid_iso_date(s) {
                Ok(Some(s.clone()))
            } else {
                Err(DeErr)
            }
        }
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

pub fn valid_iso_date(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    if b.len() != 10 || b[4] != b'-' || b[7] != b'-' {
        return false;
    }
    let num = |from: usize, to: usize| s.get(from..to).and_then(|x| x.parse::<u32>().ok());
    let (y, m, d) = match (num(0, 4), num(5, 7), num(8, 10)) {
        (Some(y), Some(m), Some(d)) => (y, m, d),
        _ => return false,
    };
    if !(1..=12).contains(&m) || d < 1 {
        return false;
    }
    let leap = (y % 4 == 0 && y % 100 != 0) || y % 400 == 0;
    let max = match m {
        1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 12 => 31,
        4 | 6 | 9 | 11 => 30,
        2 => {
            if leap {
                29
            } else {
                28
            }
        }
        _ => 0,
    };
    d <= max
}

/// `java.awt.geom.Point2D$Double` deserialization: public fields x/y,
/// defaults 0.0/0.0, unknown keys rejected.
fn jpoint(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<(f64, f64)>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Obj(_) => {
            let o = obj(v)?;
            let mut x = 0.0f64;
            let mut y = 0.0f64;
            for (k, val) in o.iter() {
                match k.as_str() {
                    "x" => {
                        x = jdouble(val)?.unwrap_or(0.0);
                    }
                    "y" => {
                        y = jdouble(val)?.unwrap_or(0.0);
                    }
                    _ => return Err(DeErr),
                }
            }
            Ok(Some((x, y)))
        }
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

pub fn apply_role(r: &mut Role, v: &JVal) -> Result<(), DeErr> {
    let o = obj(v)?;
    for (k, val) in o.iter() {
        match k.as_str() {
            "id" => r.id = jint(val)?,
            "name" => r.name = jstr(val)?,
            "description" => r.description = jstr(val)?,
            other if IGNORED.contains(&other) => {}
            _ => return Err(DeErr),
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn role_from_json(v: &JVal) -> Result<Role, DeErr> {
    let mut r = Role::default();
    apply_role(&mut r, v)?;
    Ok(r)
}

fn roles_from_json(v: &JVal) -> Result<Option<Vec<Role>>, DeErr> {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => Ok(None),
        JVal::Arr(a) => {
            let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(a.len());
            for e in a {
                out.push(role_from_json(e)?);
            }
            // the deserialized instances are all `equal()` (the `created`
            // field is ignored and stays null), so the target HashSet keeps
            // only the first element
            truncate_entity_set(&mut out);
            Ok(Some(out))
        }
        _ => Err(DeErr),
    }
}

/// `Set` semantics over entities whose `equals()` compares the class and
/// the @JsonIgnore `created` timestamp: all JSON-deserialized instances of
/// one type are equal, so only the first survives.
fn truncate_entity_set<T>(v: &mut Vec<T>) {
    if v.len() > 1 {
        v.truncate(1);
    }
}

pub fn apply_user(u: &mut User, v: &JVal) -> Result<(), DeErr> {
    let o = obj(v)?;
    for (k, val) in o.iter() {
        match k.as_str() {
            "id" => u.id = jint(val)?,
            "firstName" => u.first_name = jstr(val)?,
            "lastName" => u.last_name = jstr(val)?,
            "email" => u.email = jstr(val)?,
            "birthday" => u.birthday = jdate(val)?,
            "language" => match val {
                JVal::Null => u.language = None,
                JVal::Str(s) => u.language = Some(s.clone()),
                _ => return Err(DeErr),
            },
            "accountName" => u.account_name = jstr(val)?,

        for (i, x) in chunk.iter().enumerate() {
            n |= (*x as u32) << (16 - 8 * i);
        }
        let has = chunk.len();
        out.push(T[((n >> 18) & 63) as usize] as char);
        out.push(T[((n >> 12) & 63) as usize] as char);
        out.push(if has > 1 { T[((n >> 6) & 63) as usize] as char } else { '=' });
        out.push(if has > 2 { T[(n & 63) as usize] as char } else { '=' });
    }
    out
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Resp {
    pub status: u16,
    /// status line text; `None` falls back to the standard reason phrase
    pub status_message: Option<String>,
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub body: Vec<u8>,
}

impl Resp {
    pub fn json(status: u16, body: String) -> Resp {
        Resp {
            status,
            status_message: None,
            headers: vec![("Content-Type".into(), "application/json;charset=utf-8".into())],
            body: body.into_bytes(),
        }
    }

    pub fn empty(status: u16) -> Resp {
        Resp { status, status_message: None, headers: Vec::new(), body: Vec::new() }
    }

    /// Jetty renders its HTML error page only for requests whose body a
    /// client would actually look at (GET/HEAD/POST); other methods get an
    /// empty body without content headers.
    fn page(req: &Req, status: u16, reason: &str) -> Resp {
        if page_rendered(&req.method) {
            Resp {
                status,
                status_message: None,
                headers: vec![
                    ("Content-Type".into(), "text/html;charset=iso-8859-1".into()),
                    ("Cache-Control".into(), "must-revalidate,no-cache,no-store".into()),
                ],
                body: errorpage::page(status, reason, &req.raw_path),
            }
        } else {
            Resp::empty(status)
        }
    }

    fn page_500(req: &Req, cause: &str) -> Resp {
        if page_rendered(&req.method) {
            Resp {
                status: 500,
                status_message: None,
                headers: vec![
                    ("Content-Type".into(), "text/html;charset=iso-8859-1".into()),
                    ("Cache-Control".into(), "must-revalidate,no-cache,no-store".into()),
                ],
                body: errorpage::page_500(&req.raw_path, cause),
            }
        } else {
            Resp::empty(500)
        }
    }

    fn method_not_allowed(allow: &str) -> Resp {
        let mut r = Resp::empty(405);
        r.headers.push(("Allow".into(), allow.into()));
        r
    }

    fn options(allow: &str) -> Resp {
        let mut r = Resp::empty(200);
        r.headers.push(("Allow".into(), allow.into()));
        r.headers.push(("Accept-Patch".into(), "".into()));
        r
    }
}

const RESOURCES: [&str; 6] =
    ["users", "groups", "roles", "layers", "layerdatasources", "layerappearances"];

const DATASOURCE_500: &str = "javax.servlet.ServletException: \
org.springframework.web.util.NestedServletException: Request processing failed; \
nested exception is org.hibernate.HibernateException: Could not instantiate resultclass: \
de.terrestris.shoguncore.model.layer.source.LayerDataSource";

fn sec_kind(resource: &str) -> SecKind {
    match resource {
        "users" => SecKind::User,
        "groups" => SecKind::UserGroup,
        "roles" => SecKind::Role,
        "layers" => SecKind::Layer,
        "layerdatasources" => SecKind::LayerDataSource,
        _ => SecKind::LayerAppearance,
    }
}

fn page_rendered(method: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(method.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str(), "GET" | "HEAD" | "POST")
}

fn unauthorized(req: &Req) -> Resp {
    let mut r = Resp::page(req, 401, "Unauthorized");
    r.headers.insert(0, ("WWW-Authenticate".into(), "Basic realm=\"SHOGun Realm\"".into()));
    r
}

fn forbidden(req: &Req) -> Resp {
    Resp::page(req, 403, "Forbidden")
}

/// Percent-decode a path or query component ('+' also decodes to space,
/// as Spring's query parsing does).
pub fn url_decode(s: &str) -> String {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::with_capacity(b.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < b.len() {
        match b[i] {
            b'%' if i + 2 < b.len() => {
                let hex = std::str::from_utf8(&b[i + 1..i + 3]).unwrap_or("");
                match u8::from_str_radix(hex, 16) {
                    Ok(v) => {
                        out.push(v);
                        i += 3;
                    }
                    Err(_) => {
                        out.push(b[i]);
                        i += 1;
                    }
                }
            }
            b'+' => {
                out.push(b' ');
                i += 1;
            }
            c => {
                out.push(c);
                i += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()
}

fn parse_query(q: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for part in q.split('&') {
        if part.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = match part.split_once('=') {
            Some((k, v)) => (k, v),
            None => (part, ""),
        };
        out.push((url_decode(k), url_decode(v)));
    }
    out
}

/// `EntityUtil.listFromCommaSeparatedStringList` over all `output:only`
/// parameter values.
fn restrict_values(query: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut vals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (k, v) in query {
        if k.eq_ignore_ascii_case("output:only") {
            for piece in v.split(',') {
                vals.push(piece.trim().to_string());
            }
        }
    }
    vals
}

fn determine_restriction(query: &[(String, String)], resource: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let vals = restrict_values(query);
    if vals.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let refs: Vec<&str> = vals.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
    determine_restrict_fields(&refs, resource)
}

/// `Sets` flags from the JSON keys present in a PUT body.
fn sets_from_json(resource: &str, v: &JVal) -> Sets {
    let mut s = Sets::default();
    if let JVal::Obj(o) = v {
        let has = |k: &str| o.iter().any(|(kk, _)| kk == k);
        match resource {
            "users" => {
                s.roles = has("roles");
                s.user_groups = has("userGroups");
            }
            "groups" => {
                s.owner = has("owner");
                s.members = has("members");
                s.group_roles = has("roles");
            }
            "layers" => {
                s.appearance = has("appearance");
                s.source = has("source");
            }
            "layerappearances" => {
                s.properties = has("properties");
            }
            "layerdatasources" => {
                s.tile_grid = has("tileGrid");
                s.urls = has("urls");
                s.resolutions = has("resolutions");
                s.extent = has("extent");
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    s
}

/// Main entry: perform authentication, URL authorization and dispatch.
pub async fn route(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req) -> Resp {
    let path = req.path.trim_end_matches('/');
    let path = if path.is_empty() { "/".to_string() } else { path.to_string() };
    let segs: Vec<&str> = path.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect();

    if segs.first().copied() != Some("rest") {
        // Outside the ported slice the original serves its webapp;
        // not part of the contract.
        return Resp::page(req, 404, "Not Found");
    }

    let resource = segs.get(1).copied().unwrap_or("");
    let in_slice = RESOURCES.contains(&resource);

    let auth = match security::authenticate(&ctx.pool, req.header("authorization")).await {
        Some(a) => a,
        None => return unauthorized(req),
    };

    let needed = if in_slice {
        security::DEFAULT_USER_ROLE
    } else {
        security::SUPER_ADMIN_ROLE
    };
    if !auth.has_role_with_hierarchy(needed) {
        return forbidden(req);
    }

    if !in_slice {
        return Resp::page(req, 404, "Not Found");
    }

    let method = req.method.as_str();
    let id_seg = segs.get(2).copied();
    let sub = segs.get(3).copied();
    let id: Option<i32> = id_seg.and_then(|s| s.parse::<i32>().ok());
    let id_ok = id.is_some();

    // Method dispatch follows Spring's URL-pattern-first resolution: a
    // matched pattern with an unsupported method yields 405 even when the
    // path variable is not numeric. OPTIONS is answered by Spring's default
    // handler with the sorted set of supported methods.
    match (segs.len(), id_seg, sub) {
        (2, _, _) => match method {
            "GET" => find_all(ctx, req, &auth, resource).await,
            "POST" => create(ctx, req, &auth, resource).await,
            "OPTIONS" => Resp::options("GET,HEAD,POST,OPTIONS"),
            _ => Resp::method_not_allowed("GET, POST"),
        },
        (3, Some("filter"), _) => {
            if method == "GET" {
                find_by_filter(ctx, req, &auth, resource).await
            } else if method == "OPTIONS" {
                Resp::options("GET,HEAD,OPTIONS")
            } else {
                Resp::method_not_allowed("GET")
            }
        }
        (3, _, _) => {
            if method == "OPTIONS" {
                return Resp::options("DELETE,GET,HEAD,OPTIONS,PUT");
            }
            if !matches!(method, "GET" | "PUT" | "DELETE") {
                return Resp::method_not_allowed("DELETE, PUT, GET");
            }
            if !id_ok {
                // @PathVariable Integer conversion failure: 400
                return Resp::page(req, 400, "Bad Request");
            }
            let id = id.unwrap();
            match method {
                "GET" => find_by_id(ctx, req, &auth, resource, id).await,
                "PUT" => update(ctx, req, &auth, resource, id).await,
                "DELETE" => delete(ctx, req, &auth, resource, id).await,
                _ => unreachable!(),
            }
        }
        (4, _, Some("userGroups")) if resource == "users" => {
            if method == "OPTIONS" {
                return Resp::options("GET,HEAD,OPTIONS");
            }
            if method != "GET" {
                return Resp::method_not_allowed("GET")
            }
            if !id_ok {
                return Resp::page(req, 400, "Bad Request");
            }
            user_groups(ctx, req, &auth, id.unwrap()).await
        }
        (4, _, Some("users")) if resource == "groups" => {
            if method == "OPTIONS" {
                return Resp::options("GET,HEAD,OPTIONS");
            }
            if method != "GET" {
                return Resp::method_not_allowed("GET")
            }
            if !id_ok {
                return Resp::page(req, 400, "Bad Request");
            }
            group_users(ctx, req, &auth, id.unwrap()).await
        }
        (4, _, Some(rel)) if id_seg.is_some() => {
            let _ = rel;
            if !id_ok {
                return Resp::page(req, 400, "Bad Request");
            }
            Resp::page(req, 404, "Not Found")
        }
        _ => Resp::page(req, 404, "Not Found"),
    }
}

async fn can_read(ctx: &Ctx, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str, id: i32) -> bool {
    if auth.is_super_admin() {
        return true;
    }
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    security::has_permission(&client, auth, id, sec_kind(resource), Permission::Read)
        .await
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

    if auth.is_super_admin() {
        return true;
    }
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    security::has_permission(&client, auth, id, sec_kind(resource), perm)
        .await
        .unwrap_or(false)
}

use crate::repo::{
    load_appearance, load_data_source, load_group, load_layer, load_role, load_user,
};

pub enum LoadedEntity {
    User(User),
    Group(UserGroup),
    Role(Role),
    Layer(Layer),
    DataSource(LayerDataSource),
    Appearance(LayerAppearance),
}

impl LoadedEntity {
    fn write_json(&self, out: &mut String) {
        match self {
            LoadedEntity::User(e) => write_user(out, e),
            LoadedEntity::Group(e) => write_user_group(out, e),
            LoadedEntity::Role(e) => write_role(out, e),
            LoadedEntity::Layer(e) => write_layer(out, e),
            LoadedEntity::DataSource(e) => write_layer_data_source(out, e),
            LoadedEntity::Appearance(e) => write_layer_appearance(out, e),
        }
    }

    fn id(&self) -> i32 {
        match self {
            LoadedEntity::User(e) => e.id.unwrap_or(0),
            LoadedEntity::Group(e) => e.id.unwrap_or(0),
            LoadedEntity::Role(e) => e.id.unwrap_or(0),
            LoadedEntity::Layer(e) => e.id.unwrap_or(0),
            LoadedEntity::DataSource(e) => e.base.id.unwrap_or(0),
            LoadedEntity::Appearance(e) => e.id.unwrap_or(0),
        }
    }

    fn restrict(&mut self, fields: &[String]) {
        match self {
            LoadedEntity::User(e) => e.restrict(fields),
            LoadedEntity::Group(e) => e.restrict(fields),
            LoadedEntity::Role(e) => e.restrict(fields),
            LoadedEntity::Layer(e) => e.restrict(fields),
            LoadedEntity::Appearance(e) => e.restrict(fields),
            LoadedEntity::DataSource(_) => unreachable!("abstract projection fails first"),
        }
    }
}

async fn load_entity(
    client: &tokio_postgres::Client,
    resource: &str,
    id: i32,
) -> repo::LR<Option<LoadedEntity>> {
    Ok(match resource {
        "users" => load_user(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::User),
        "groups" => load_group(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::Group),
        "roles" => load_role(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::Role),
        "layers" => load_layer(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::Layer),
        "layerdatasources" => load_data_source(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::DataSource),
        _ => load_appearance(client, id).await?.map(LoadedEntity::Appearance),
    })
}

fn list_response(ents: Vec<LoadedEntity>) -> Resp {
    let mut out = String::from("[");
    for (i, e) in ents.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            out.push(',');
        }
        e.write_json(&mut out);
    }
    out.push(']');
    Resp::json(200, out)
}

async fn find_all(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str) -> Resp {
    let restrict = determine_restriction(&req.query, resource);
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };
    let ids = match repo::list_ids(&client, resource).await {
        Ok(ids) => ids,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
    };
    // Transformers.aliasToBean(LayerDataSource) fails while transforming
    // the FIRST result row: with at least one row the request is a 500.
    if resource == "layerdatasources" && restrict.is_some() && !ids.is_empty() {
        return Resp::page_500(req, DATASOURCE_500);
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for id in ids {
        let loaded = match load_entity(&client, resource, id).await {
            Ok(Some(e)) => e,
            Ok(None) => continue,
            Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
        };
        // @PostFilter READ
        if !can_read(ctx, auth, resource, id).await {
            continue;
        }
        out.push(loaded);
    }
    if let Some(fields) = &restrict {
        for e in out.iter_mut() {
            e.restrict(fields);
        }
    }
    list_response(out)
}

async fn find_by_filter(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str) -> Resp {
    let restrict = determine_restriction(&req.query, resource);
    let groups = repo::resolve_filters(resource, &req.query);
    if groups.is_empty() {
        // findBySimpleFilter starts with an empty list and only queries when
        // at least one valid filter field is present
        return Resp::json(200, "[]".to_string());
    }
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };
    let ids = match repo::filter_ids(&client, resource, &groups).await {
        Ok(ids) => ids,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
    };
    if resource == "layerdatasources" && restrict.is_some() && !ids.is_empty() {
        return Resp::page_500(req, DATASOURCE_500);
    }
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for id in ids {
        let loaded = match load_entity(&client, resource, id).await {
            Ok(Some(e)) => e,
            Ok(None) => continue,
            Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
        };
        if !can_read(ctx, auth, resource, id).await {
            continue;
        }
        out.push(loaded);
    }
    if let Some(fields) = &restrict {
        for e in out.iter_mut() {
            e.restrict(fields);
        }
    }
    list_response(out)
}

async fn find_by_id(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str, id: i32) -> Resp {
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };
    let loaded = match load_entity(&client, resource, id).await {
        Ok(e) => e,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
    };
    let entity = match loaded {
        Some(e) => e,
        // @PostAuthorize on a null returnObject denies for non-admins, and
        // the admin path ends in an NPE: both are caught -> 404
        None => return Resp::empty(404),
    };
    if !can_read(ctx, auth, resource, id).await {
        return Resp::empty(404);
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    entity.write_json(&mut out);
    Resp::json(200, out)
}

/// `UserGroupIdResolver` semantics: a `userGroups` reference to a missing
/// id fails the JSON deserialization itself, so no write (and no id
/// allocation) happens at all.
async fn group_refs_valid(ctx: &Ctx, u: &User) -> bool {
    let gids = match &u.user_groups {
        Some(g) => g,
        None => return true,
    };
    if gids.is_empty() {
        return true;
    }
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return false,
    };
    let rows = client
        .query(
            "SELECT id FROM usergroups WHERE id = ANY($1)",
            &[&gids.as_slice()],
        )
        .await;
    match rows {
        Ok(rows) => rows.len() >= dedup_len(gids),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

fn dedup_len(v: &[i32]) -> usize {
    let mut seen: Vec<i32> = Vec::new();
    for x in v {
        if !seen.contains(x) {
            seen.push(*x);
        }
    }
    seen.len()
}

async fn user_groups(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, id: i32) -> Resp {
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };
    // `this.findById(userId)` is a self-invocation inside
    // `getGroupsOfUser`, so no READ check happens for the USER itself; the
    // returned groups are still subject to the method's @PostFilter.
    let user = match load_user(&client, id).await {
        Ok(Some(u)) => u,
        Ok(None) => return Resp::empty(404),
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
    };
    let mut out = String::from("[");
    let gids = user.user_groups.unwrap_or_default();
    let mut first = true;
    for gid in gids.iter() {
        let g = match load_group(&client, *gid).await {
            Ok(Some(g)) => g,
            Ok(None) => continue,
            Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
        };
        // @PostFilter READ on each group
        if !auth.is_super_admin() && !can_read(ctx, auth, "groups", *gid).await {
            continue;
        }
        if !first {
            out.push(',');
        }
        first = false;
        write_user_group(&mut out, &g);
    }
    out.push(']');
    Resp::json(200, out)
}

async fn group_users(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, id: i32) -> Resp {
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };
    // same self-invocation quirk as /users/{id}/userGroups; the members
    // are subject to the method's @PostFilter READ
    let group = match load_group(&client, id).await {
        Ok(Some(g)) => g,
        Ok(None) => return Resp::empty(404),
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "database error"),
    };
    let mut out = String::from("[");
    let members = group.members.unwrap_or_default();
    let mut first = true;
    for u in members.iter() {
        let uid = u.id.unwrap_or(0);
        if !auth.is_super_admin() && !can_read(ctx, auth, "users", uid).await {
            continue;
        }
        if !first {
            out.push(',');
        }
        first = false;
        write_user(&mut out, u);
    }
    out.push(']');
    Resp::json(200, out)
}

// -------------------------------------------------------------------- create

async fn create(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str) -> Resp {
    // The abstract LayerDataSource cannot be built from JSON at all.
    if resource == "layerdatasources" {
        return Resp::empty(400);
    }
    let val = match parse(&req.body) {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
    };
    // @PreAuthorize CREATE: a transient entity has no permission
    // collections, so only the super admin can ever create.
    if !auth.is_super_admin() {
        return Resp::empty(400);
    }
    let mut ent: LoadedEntity = match resource {
        "users" => match de::user_from_json(&val) {
            Ok(u) => LoadedEntity::User(u),
            Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
        },
        "groups" => match de::group_from_json(&val) {
            Ok(g) => LoadedEntity::Group(g),
            Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
        },
        "roles" => match de::role_from_json(&val) {
            Ok(r) => LoadedEntity::Role(r),
            Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
        },
        "layers" => match de::layer_from_json(&val) {
            Ok(l) => LoadedEntity::Layer(l),
            Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
        },
        _ => match de::appearance_from_json(&val) {
            Ok(a) => LoadedEntity::Appearance(a),
            Err(_) => return Resp::empty(400),
        },
    };
    // ID value MUST be null
    let has_id = match &ent {
        LoadedEntity::User(e) => e.id.is_some(),
        LoadedEntity::Group(e) => e.id.is_some(),
        LoadedEntity::Role(e) => e.id.is_some(),
        LoadedEntity::Layer(e) => e.id.is_some(),
        LoadedEntity::Appearance(e) => e.id.is_some(),
        LoadedEntity::DataSource(_) => false,
    };
    if has_id {
        return Resp::empty(400);
    }
    if let LoadedEntity::User(u) = &ent {
        if !group_refs_valid(ctx, u).await {
            return Resp::empty(400);
        }
    }
    let sets = sets_from_json(resource, &val);
    match write_entity(ctx, resource, &mut ent, &sets, None, true).await {
        Ok(()) => {
            let mut out = String::new();
            ent.write_json(&mut out);
            Resp::json(201, out)
        }
        Err(_) => Resp::empty(400),
    }
}

async fn update(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str, id: i32) -> Resp {
    // an empty body deserializes to a null tree ("no 'id' property"): 400
    if req.body.iter().all(|b| b.is_ascii_whitespace()) {
        return Resp::empty(400);
    }
    // readTree: malformed JSON -> catch -> 404
    let val = match parse(&req.body) {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => return Resp::empty(404),
    };
    // the JSON object must carry an id equal to the path variable
    let payload_id = match &val {
        JVal::Obj(_) => Some(val.get("id").map(|v| v.as_java_int().unwrap_or(0)).unwrap_or(0)),
        _ => None,
    };
    match payload_id {
        None => return Resp::empty(400),
        Some(pid) if pid != id as i64 => return Resp::empty(400),
        _ => {}
    }
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),
    };

    let loaded = match load_entity(&client, resource, id).await {
        Ok(e) => e,
        Err(_) => return Resp::empty(404),
    };
    let mut ent = match loaded {
        Some(e) => e,
        None => return Resp::empty(404),
    };
    if !can_read(ctx, auth, resource, id).await {
        return Resp::empty(404);
    }
    // @PreAuthorize UPDATE
    if !can_write(ctx, auth, resource, id, Permission::Update).await {
        return Resp::empty(404);
    }
    // the session identities are those of the initially loaded graph
    // (captured before the JSON replaces any associations)
    let sess = session_ids(&ent);
    // readerForUpdating(entity): JSON onto the loaded instance
    let sets = sets_from_json(resource, &val);
    let applied = match &mut ent {
        LoadedEntity::User(e) => de::apply_user(e, &val),
        LoadedEntity::Group(e) => de::apply_user_group(e, &val),
        LoadedEntity::Role(e) => de::apply_role(e, &val),
        LoadedEntity::Layer(e) => de::apply_layer(e, &val),
        LoadedEntity::Appearance(e) => de::apply_layer_appearance(e, &val),
        LoadedEntity::DataSource(e) => de::apply_layer_data_source(e, &val),
    };
    if applied.is_err() {
        // Jackson applies fields one by one; when it fails mid-object the
        // session-attached entity keeps the *scalar* fields applied so far
        // (collection/nested properties are only assigned once their value
        // is fully deserialized), and the OpenSessionInView auto-flush
        // persists them even though the request is answered with 404.
        flush_entity(ctx, resource, &ent).await;

        if !group_refs_valid(ctx, u).await {
            // the failing userGroups reference never completed: the
            // collection keeps its loaded value, only scalars flush
            flush_entity(ctx, resource, &ent).await;
            return Resp::empty(404);
        }
    }
    match write_entity(ctx, resource, &mut ent, &sets, Some(&sess), false).await {
        Ok(()) => {
            let mut out = String::new();
            ent.write_json(&mut out);
            Resp::json(200, out)
        }
        Err(_) => Resp::empty(404),
    }
}

fn session_ids(ent: &LoadedEntity) -> SessionIds {
    match ent {
        LoadedEntity::Layer(l) => SessionIds::of_layer(l),
        LoadedEntity::DataSource(d) => SessionIds::of_datasource(d),
        _ => SessionIds::default(),
    }
}

async fn delete(ctx: &Ctx, req: &Req, auth: &AuthUser, resource: &str, id: i32) -> Resp {
    let client = match ctx.pool.get().await {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Resp::page_500(req, "connection failed"),

            }

    tx_client.recycle().await;
    alloc.recycle().await;

async fn delete_entity(ctx: &Ctx, resource: &str, ent: &LoadedEntity) -> Result<(), WriteErr> {

//! Minimal HTTP/1.1 server on tokio: keep-alive, Content-Length and
//! chunked request bodies, HEAD handling.

use crate::handlers::{route, Ctx, Req, Resp};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt, BufReader};
use tokio::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};

const MAX_HEAD: usize = 64 * 1024;
const MAX_BODY: usize = 64 * 1024 * 1024;

pub async fn serve(ctx: Ctx, port: u16) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(("0.0.0.0", port)).await?;
    let ctx = Arc::new(ctx);
    loop {
        let (stream, _addr) = match listener.accept().await {
            Ok(x) => x,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        let ctx = ctx.clone();
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let _ = handle_connection(ctx, stream).await;
        });
    }
}

async fn handle_connection(ctx: Arc<Ctx>, stream: TcpStream) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    stream.set_nodelay(true).ok();
    let (read_half, mut write_half) = stream.into_split();
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(read_half);
    let mut keep_alive = true;
    while keep_alive {
        let req = match read_request(&mut reader).await? {
            Some(r) => r,
            None => return Ok(()), // clean EOF between requests
        };
        keep_alive = req.0;
        let is_head = req.1.method.eq_ignore_ascii_case("HEAD");
        let method = req.1.method.clone();
        let resp = route(&ctx, &req.1).await;
        write_response(&mut write_half, &resp, is_head, &method).await?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Read one request. Returns `None` on a clean EOF before any bytes.
async fn read_request(
    reader: &mut BufReader<tokio::net::tcp::OwnedReadHalf>,
) -> std::io::Result<Option<(bool, Req)>> {
    let mut head = Vec::with_capacity(1024);
    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
    // read until CRLFCRLF
    loop {
        let n = match reader.read(&mut byte).await {
            Ok(0) => {
                if head.is_empty() {
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, "eof in head"));
            }
            Ok(n) => n,
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        head.extend_from_slice(&byte[..n]);
        if head.len() > MAX_HEAD {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "head too large"));
        }
        if head.len() >= 4 && &head[head.len() - 4..] == b"\r\n\r\n" {
            break;
        }
        if head.len() >= 2 && &head[head.len() - 2..] == b"\n\n" {
            break;
        }
    }
    let head_text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head).into_owned();
    let mut lines = head_text.split("\r\n").flat_map(|l| l.split('\n'));
    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or("");
    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();
    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let version = parts.next().unwrap_or("HTTP/1.1").to_string();
    if method.is_empty() || target.is_empty() {
        return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "bad request line"));
    }

    let mut headers: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    for line in lines {
        if line.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {
            headers.push((k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string()));
        }
    }
    let header = |name: &str| headers.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == name).map(|(_, v)| v.clone());

    let keep_alive = match header("connection").as_deref() {
        Some(c) if c.eq_ignore_ascii_case("close") => false,
        _ if version == "HTTP/1.0" => false,
        _ => true,
    };

    // body
    let mut body: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(te) = header("transfer-encoding") {
        if te.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("chunked") {
            loop {
                // read chunk size line
                let line = read_line(reader).await?;
                let size_str = line.trim().split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim();
                let size = usize::from_str_radix(size_str, 16)
                    .map_err(|_| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "bad chunk size"))?;
                if body.len() + size > MAX_BODY {
                    return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "body too large"));
                }
                if size == 0 {
                    // trailing headers until empty line
                    loop {
                        let l = read_line(reader).await?;
                        if l.is_empty() {
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    break;
                }
                let mut chunk = vec![0u8; size];
                reader.read_exact(&mut chunk).await?;
                body.extend_from_slice(&chunk);
                // consume CRLF after chunk
                let mut crlf = [0u8; 2];
                reader.read_exact(&mut crlf).await?;
            }
        }
    } else if let Some(cl) = header("content-length") {
        let len: usize = cl
            .trim()
            .parse()
            .map_err(|_| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "bad content-length"))?;
        if len > MAX_BODY {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "body too large"));
        }
        body = vec![0u8; len];
        if len > 0 {
            reader.read_exact(&mut body).await?;
        }
    }

    // split path and query
    let (raw_path, raw_query) = match target.split_once('?') {
        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),
        None => (target.clone(), String::new()),
    };
    let decoded_path = crate::handlers::url_decode(&raw_path);
    let query = parse_query_raw(&raw_query);

    let req = Req {
        method,
        path: decoded_path,
        raw_path,
        query,
        headers,
        body,
    };
    Ok(Some((keep_alive, req)))
}

fn parse_query_raw(q: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for part in q.split('&') {
        if part.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let (k, v) = match part.split_once('=') {
            Some((k, v)) => (k, v),
            None => (part, ""),
        };
        out.push((crate::handlers::url_decode(k), crate::handlers::url_decode(v)));
    }
    out
}

async fn read_line(reader: &mut BufReader<tokio::net::tcp::OwnedReadHalf>) -> std::io::Result<String> {
    let mut line = Vec::new();
    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];
    loop {
        let n = reader.read(&mut byte).await?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        if byte[0] == b'\n' {
            break;
        }
        line.push(byte[0]);
        if line.len() > 8192 {
            return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "line too long"));
        }
    }
    let mut s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&line).into_owned();
    if s.ends_with('\r') {
        s.pop();
    }
    Ok(s)
}

fn status_text(status: u16) -> &'static str {
    match status {
        200 => "OK",
        201 => "Created",
        204 => "No Content",
        400 => "Bad Request",
        401 => "Unauthorized",
        403 => "Forbidden",
        404 => "Not Found",
        405 => "Method Not Allowed",
        500 => "Server Error",
        _ => "",
    }
}

async fn write_response(
    out: &mut tokio::net::tcp::OwnedWriteHalf,
    resp: &Resp,
    is_head: bool,
    method: &str,
) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let status_line = match (&resp.status_message, resp.status) {
        (Some(m), _) => m.clone(),
        (None, 405) => format!("405 Request method '{}' not supported", method),
        (None, s) => format!("{} {}", s, status_text(s)),
    };
    let mut head = format!("HTTP/1.1 {}\r\n", status_line);
    for (k, v) in &resp.headers {
        head.push_str(k);
        head.push_str(": ");
        head.push_str(v);
        head.push_str("\r\n");
    }
    head.push_str(&format!("Content-Length: {}\r\n", resp.body.len()));
    head.push_str("\r\n");
    out.write_all(head.as_bytes()).await?;
    if !is_head {
        out.write_all(&resp.body).await?;
    }
    out.flush().await
}

//! Codec for the Java-serialization format that Hibernate uses to persist
//! element collections of `java.awt.geom.Point2D$Double` (the XYZ layer
//! datasource's `resolutions`) and, for rows created by hand,
//! `java.lang.Double`.

/// Stream magic + version: every row is an independent
/// `ObjectOutputStream` image.
const STREAM_HEADER: [u8; 4] = [0xAC, 0xED, 0x00, 0x05];

const TC_OBJECT: u8 = 0x73;
const TC_CLASSDESC: u8 = 0x72;
const TC_ENDBLOCKDATA: u8 = 0x78;
const TC_NULL: u8 = 0x70;
const TC_STRING: u8 = 0x74;

/// The class descriptor itself (without the superclass reference).
fn classdesc_body(name: &str, uid: [u8; 8], fields: &[(u8, &str)]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    out.push(TC_CLASSDESC);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(name.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(&uid);
    out.push(0x02); // java.io.Serializable
    out.extend_from_slice(&(fields.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
    for (ty, fname) in fields {
        out.push(*ty);
        out.extend_from_slice(&(fname.len() as u16).to_be_bytes());
        out.extend_from_slice(fname.as_bytes());
    }
    out.push(TC_ENDBLOCKDATA);
    out
}

/// Descriptor of `java.lang.Number` (the superclass of Double and Integer).
fn number_classdesc() -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut v = classdesc_body(
        "java.lang.Number",
        [0x86, 0xAC, 0x95, 0x1D, 0x0B, 0x94, 0xE0, 0x8B],
        &[],
    );
    v.push(TC_NULL); // Number extends Object
    v
}

        let mut v = STREAM_HEADER.to_vec();

struct Parser<'a> {

            Some(b'{') => self.object(),
            Some(b'[') => self.array(),
            Some(b'"') => Ok(JVal::Str(self.string()?)),
            Some(b't') => self.lit(b"true", JVal::Bool(true)),
            Some(b'f') => self.lit(b"false", JVal::Bool(false)),
            Some(b'n') => self.lit(b"null", JVal::Null),

            _ => Err(ParseErr),

        if self.b.len() - self.i >= s.len() && &self.b[self.i..self.i + s.len()] == s {
            self.i += s.len();
            Ok(v)

            Err(ParseErr)

/// Jackson-style string escaping. Non-ASCII characters are written as raw UTF-8.
pub fn write_str(out: &mut String, s: &str) {
    out.push('"');
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\u{8}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\u{c}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {
                let _ = write!(out, "\\u{:04X}", c as u32);
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

/// Java `Double.toString` formatting, as used by Jackson for double values.
pub fn java_double(d: f64) -> String {
    if d.is_nan() {
        return "NaN".to_string();
    }
    if d.is_infinite() {
        return if d > 0.0 { "Infinity".to_string() } else { "-Infinity".to_string() };
    }
    if d == 0.0 {
        return if d.is_sign_negative() { "-0.0".to_string() } else { "0.0".to_string() };
    }
    // Rust's LowerExp gives the shortest round-trip representation.
    let s = format!("{:e}", d);
    let (mant, exps) = s.split_once('e').expect("exp");
    let exp: i32 = exps.parse().expect("exp int");
    let neg = mant.starts_with('-');
    let mant = mant.trim_start_matches('-');
    let digits: String = mant.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let digits = digits.as_str();

    let mut body = String::new();
    if (-3..=6).contains(&exp) {
        // plain decimal notation
        if exp >= 0 {
            let ip = (exp as usize) + 1;
            if digits.len() > ip {
                body.push_str(&digits[..ip]);
                body.push('.');
                body.push_str(&digits[ip..]);
            } else {
                body.push_str(digits);
                for _ in digits.len()..ip {
                    body.push('0');
                }
                body.push_str(".0");
            }
        } else {
            body.push_str("0.");
            for _ in 0..(-exp - 1) {
                body.push('0');
            }
            body.push_str(digits);
        }
    } else {
        // computerized scientific notation, Java style: D.DDE±X
        body.push_str(&digits[..1]);
        body.push('.');
        if digits.len() > 1 {
            body.push_str(&digits[1..]);
        } else {
            body.push('0');
        }
        body.push('E');
        let _ = write!(body, "{}", exp);
    }
    if neg {
        format!("-{}", body)
    } else {
        body
    }
}

pub fn write_double(out: &mut String, d: f64) {
    out.push_str(&java_double(d));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- writing

fn wi(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: &Option<i32>, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    match v {
        Some(i) => out.push_str(&i.to_string()),
        None => out.push_str("null"),
    }
}

fn wb(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: bool, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    out.push_str(if v { "true" } else { "false" });
}

fn wbo(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: &Option<bool>, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    match v {
        Some(b) => out.push_str(if *b { "true" } else { "false" }),
        None => out.push_str("null"),
    }
}

fn ws(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: &Option<String>, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    match v {
        Some(s) => write_str(out, s),
        None => out.push_str("null"),
    }
}

fn wd(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: &Option<f64>, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    match v {
        Some(d) => {
            if d.is_nan() || d.is_infinite() {
                // Jackson quotes non-finite doubles
                out.push('"');
                out.push_str(&java_double(*d));
                out.push('"');
            } else {
                out.push_str(&java_double(*d));
            }
        }
        None => out.push_str("null"),
    }
}

fn key(out: &mut String, name: &str, first: bool) {
    if !first {
        out.push(',');
    }
    write_str(out, name);
    out.push(':');
}

fn wpoint(out: &mut String, name: &str, v: &Option<(f64, f64)>, first: bool) {
    key(out, name, first);
    match v {
        Some((x, y)) => {
            out.push_str("{\"x\":");
            write_num(out, *x);
            out.push_str(",\"y\":");
            write_num(out, *y);
            out.push('}');
        }
        None => out.push_str("null"),
    }
}

fn write_num(out: &mut String, d: f64) {
    if d.is_nan() || d.is_infinite() {
        out.push('"');
        out.push_str(&java_double(d));
        out.push('"');
    } else {
        out.push_str(&java_double(d));
    }
}

pub fn write_role(out: &mut String, r: &Role) {

    ws(out, "name", &r.name, false);

}

fn write_roles(out: &mut String, roles: &Option<Vec<Role>>) {
    match roles {
        None => out.push_str("null"),
        Some(v) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, r) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_role(out, r);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
    }
}

fn write_doubles(out: &mut String, v: &[f64]) {
    out.push('[');
    for (i, d) in v.iter().enumerate() {
        if i > 0 {
            out.push(',');
        }
        if d.is_nan() || d.is_infinite() {
            out.push('"');
            out.push_str(&java_double(*d));
            out.push('"');
        } else {
            out.push_str(&java_double(*d));
        }
    }
    out.push(']');
}

pub fn write_tile_grid(out: &mut String, t: &TileGrid) {
    out.push('{');
    wi(out, "id", &t.id, true);
    ws(out, "type", &t.typ, false);
    wpoint(out, "tileGridOrigin", &t.origin, false);
    key(out, "tileGridExtent", false);
    match &t.extent {
        None => out.push_str("null"),
        Some(e) => write_extent(out, e),
    }
    wi(out, "tileSize", &t.tile_size, false);
    key(out, "tileGridResolutions", false);
    match &t.resolutions {
        None => out.push_str("null"),
        Some(v) => write_doubles(out, v),
    }
    if t.is_wmts {
        key(out, "matrixIds", false);
        match &t.matrix_ids {
            None => out.push_str("null"),
            Some(v) => {
                out.push('[');
                for (i, s) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i > 0 {
                        out.push(',');
                    }
                    write_str(out, s);
                }
                out.push(']');
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('}');
}

pub fn write_layer_appearance(out: &mut String, a: &LayerAppearance) {
    out.push('{');
    wi(out, "id", &a.id, true);
    ws(out, "attribution", &a.attribution, false);
    wbo(out, "hoverable", &a.hoverable, false);
    wbo(out, "clickable", &a.clickable, false);
    ws(out, "hoverTemplate", &a.hover_template, false);
    key(out, "properties", false);
    match &a.properties {
        None => out.push_str("null"),
        Some(v) => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, val)) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_str(out, k);
                out.push(':');
                out.push_str(&jval_to_json(val));
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
    ws(out, "name", &a.name, false);
    wd(out, "maxResolution", &a.max_resolution, false);
    wd(out, "minResolution", &a.min_resolution, false);
    wd(out, "opacity", &a.opacity, false);
    wbo(out, "visible", &a.visible, false);
    out.push('}');
}

pub fn jval_to_json(v: &JVal) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    write_jval(&mut out, v);
    out
}

pub fn write_jval(out: &mut String, v: &JVal) {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => out.push_str("null"),
        JVal::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { "true" } else { "false" }),
        JVal::Int(i) => out.push_str(&i.to_string()),
        JVal::Float(f) => {
            if f.is_nan() || f.is_infinite() {
                out.push('"');
                out.push_str(&java_double(*f));
                out.push('"');
            } else {
                out.push_str(&java_double(*f));
            }
        }
        JVal::Str(s) => write_str(out, s),
        JVal::Arr(a) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, v) in a.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_jval(out, v);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        JVal::Obj(o) => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, v)) in o.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_str(out, k);
                out.push(':');
                write_jval(out, v);
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
}

pub fn write_layer_data_source(out: &mut String, d: &LayerDataSource) {
    out.push('{');
    let b = &d.base;
    wi(out, "id", &b.id, true);
    ws(out, "name", &b.name, false);
    ws(out, "type", &b.typ, false);
    ws(out, "url", &b.url, false);
    ws(out, "format", &b.format, false);
    match d.kind() {
        DsKind::ImageWms | DsKind::TileWms => {
            if let Some(im) = &d.image_wms {
                out.push_str(",\"width\":");
                out.push_str(&im.width.to_string());
                out.push_str(",\"height\":");
                out.push_str(&im.height.to_string());
                ws(out, "version", &im.version, false);
                ws(out, "layerNames", &im.layer_names, false);
                ws(out, "layerStyles", &im.layer_styles, false);
                wbo(out, "requestableByPath", &im.requestable_by_path, false);
                ws(out, "customRequestPath", &im.custom_request_path, false);
            }
            if d.kind() == DsKind::TileWms {
                if let Some(t) = &d.tile_wms {
                    key(out, "tileGrid", false);
                    match &t.tile_grid {
                        None => out.push_str("null"),
                        Some(tg) => write_tile_grid(out, tg),
                    }
                    wbo(out, "requestWithTiled", &t.request_with_tiled, false);
                }
            }
        }
        DsKind::Wfs => {
            if let Some(w) = &d.wfs {
                ws(out, "version", &w.version, false);
                ws(out, "typeName", &w.type_name, false);
                ws(out, "typeNames", &w.type_names, false);
            }
        }
        DsKind::Wmts => {
            if let Some(m) = &d.wmts {
                key(out, "tileGrid", false);
                match &m.tile_grid {
                    None => out.push_str("null"),
                    Some(tg) => write_tile_grid(out, tg),
                }
                key(out, "urls", false);
                match &m.urls {
                    None => out.push_str("null"),
                    Some(v) => {
                        out.push('[');
                        for (i, s) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                            if i > 0 {
                                out.push(',');
                            }
                            write_str(out, s);
                        }
                        out.push(']');
                    }
                }
                ws(out, "wmtsLayer", &m.wmts_layer, false);
                ws(out, "wmtsStyle", &m.wmts_style, false);
                ws(out, "projection", &m.projection, false);
                ws(out, "matrixSet", &m.matrix_set, false);
                ws(out, "requestEncoding", &m.request_encoding, false);
                ws(out, "capabilitiesUrl", &m.capabilities_url, false);
            }
        }
        DsKind::Xyz => {
            if let Some(x) = &d.xyz {
                wpoint(out, "center", &x.center, false);
                key(out, "extent", false);
                match &x.extent {
                    None => out.push_str("null"),
                    Some(e) => write_extent(out, e),
                }
                key(out, "resolutions", false);
                match &x.resolutions {
                    None => out.push_str("null"),
                    Some(v) => {
                        out.push('[');
                        for (i, r) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                            if i > 0 {
                                out.push(',');
                            }
                            match r {
                                XyzRes::Point(px, py) => {
                                    out.push_str("{\"x\":");
                                    write_num(out, *px);
                                    out.push_str(",\"y\":");
                                    write_num(out, *py);
                                    out.push('}');
                                }
                                XyzRes::Double(f) => write_num(out, *f),
                                XyzRes::Integer(n) => out.push_str(&n.to_string()),
                                XyzRes::Str(s) => write_str(out, s),
                            }
                        }
                        out.push(']');
                    }
                }
                wi(out, "tileSize", &x.tile_size, false);
            }
        }
    }
    out.push('}');
}

/// The filterable/restrictable (non-static private primitive/wrapper/String)
/// field names, in `EntityUtil.getFilterableOrRestrictableFieldNames` order.
pub fn restrictable_fields(resource: &str) -> &'static [&'static str] {
    match resource {
        "users" => &["id", "firstName", "lastName", "email", "accountName", "password", "active"],
        "groups" => &["id", "name"],
        "roles" => &["id", "name", "description"],
        "layers" => &["id", "name", "description"],
        "layerdatasources" => &["id", "name", "type", "url", "format"],
        "layerappearances" => &[
            "id",
            "attribution",
            "hoverable",
            "clickable",
            "hoverTemplate",
            "name",
            "maxResolution",
            "minResolution",
            "opacity",
            "visible",
        ],
        _ => &[],
    }
}

/// Case-insensitive intersection of requested and restrictable field names,
/// keeping the canonical (Java) casing. `None` when nothing matches, meaning
/// "no restriction".
pub fn determine_restrict_fields(requested: &[&str], resource: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let restrictable = restrictable_fields(resource);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for f in restrictable {
        if requested.iter().any(|r| f.eq_ignore_ascii_case(r)) {
            out.push(f.to_string());
        }
    }
    if out.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(out)
    }
}

impl User {
    /// Reset every field not in `fields` to its Java constructor default
    /// (what Hibernate's aliasToBean projection would produce).
    pub fn restrict(&mut self, fields: &[String]) {
        let has = |n: &str| fields.iter().any(|f| f == n);
        if !has("id") {
            self.id = None;
        }
        if !has("firstName") {
            self.first_name = None;
        }
        if !has("lastName") {
            self.last_name = None;
        }
        if !has("email") {
            self.email = None;
        }
        if !has("accountName") {
            self.account_name = None;
        }
        if !has("password") {
            self.password = None;
        }
        if !has("active") {
            self.active = false;
        }
        // not restrictable: constructor-initialized empty collections
        self.birthday = None;
        self.language = None;
        self.roles = Some(Vec::new());
        self.user_groups = Some(Vec::new());
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum FilterVal {
    Int(i32),
    Str(String),
    Bool(bool),
    Double(f64),
    /// Value could not be cast: matches nothing (`eq(field, null)`).
    None,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum FieldType {
    Int,
    Str,
    BoolPrim,
    BoolWrap,
    Double,
}

pub fn filter_field_type(resource: &str, field: &str) -> Option<FieldType> {
    let fields = restrictable_fields(resource);
    let f = fields.iter().find(|f| f.eq_ignore_ascii_case(field))?;
    let resource = resource;
    Some(match (resource, f.as_ref()) {
        (_, "id") => FieldType::Int,
        (_, "active") => FieldType::BoolPrim,
        (_, "hoverable") | (_, "clickable") | (_, "visible") => FieldType::BoolWrap,
        (_, "maxResolution") | (_, "minResolution") | (_, "opacity") => FieldType::Double,
        _ => FieldType::Str,
    })
}

/// commons-beanutils `ConvertUtils.convert(value, targetType)` semantics.
pub fn cast_filter_value(ft: FieldType, raw: &str) -> FilterVal {
    match ft {
        FieldType::Str => FilterVal::Str(raw.to_string()),
        FieldType::Int => match raw.parse::<i64>() {
            Ok(v) if v >= i32::MIN as i64 && v <= i32::MAX as i64 => FilterVal::Int(v as i32),
            _ => FilterVal::None,
        },
        FieldType::Double => match raw.parse::<f64>() {
            Ok(v) => FilterVal::Double(v),
            Err(_) => FilterVal::None,
        },
        FieldType::BoolPrim | FieldType::BoolWrap => {
            let l = raw.to_ascii_lowercase();
            if ["true", "yes", "y", "on", "1"].contains(&l.as_str()) {
                FilterVal::Bool(true)
            } else if ["false", "no", "n", "off", "0"].contains(&l.as_str()) {
                FilterVal::Bool(false)
            } else if ft == FieldType::BoolPrim {
                // BooleanConverter default for the primitive type: false
                FilterVal::Bool(false)
            } else {
                FilterVal::None
            }

/// `PropertyValueConverter.convertToEntityAttribute`: string from the DB to
/// the best matching JSON type.
pub fn property_from_db(s: &str) -> JVal {
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("true") {
        return JVal::Bool(true);
    }
    if s.eq_ignore_ascii_case("false") {
        return JVal::Bool(false);
    }
    if is_parsable(s) {
        let digits = |x: &str| !x.is_empty() && x.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit());
        if digits(s) || (s.starts_with('-') && digits(&s[1..])) {
            if let Ok(v) = s.parse::<i64>() {
                return JVal::Int(v);
            }
        } else if let Ok(v) = s.parse::<f64>() {
            return JVal::Float(v);
        }
    }
    JVal::Str(s.to_string())
}

/// commons-lang3 `NumberUtils.isParsable`.
pub fn is_parsable(s: &str) -> bool {
    if s.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let start = if b[0] == b'-' {
        if b.len() == 1 {
            return false;
        }
        1
    } else {
        0
    };
    let mut points = 0;
    for &c in &b[start..] {
        if c == b'.' {
            points += 1;
            if points > 1 {
                return false;
            }
        } else if !c.is_ascii_digit() {
            return false;
        }
    }
    true
}

/// `attribute.toString()` for a deserialized JSON property value
/// (Java `Object.toString` of String/Long/Double/Boolean/LinkedHashMap...).
pub fn property_to_db(v: &JVal) -> String {
    match v {
        JVal::Null => "null".to_string(),
        JVal::Bool(b) => b.to_string(),
        JVal::Int(i) => i.to_string(),
        JVal::Float(f) => crate::json::java_double(*f),
        JVal::Str(s) => s.clone(),
        JVal::Arr(a) => {
            let mut out = String::from("[");
            for (i, e) in a.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push_str(", ");
                }
                out.push_str(&property_to_db(e));
            }
            out.push(']');
            out
        }
        JVal::Obj(o) => {
            let mut out = String::from("{");
            for (i, (k, e)) in o.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push_str(", ");
                }
                out.push_str(k);
                out.push('=');
                out.push_str(&property_to_db(e));
            }
            out.push('}');
            out
        }
    }
}

pub struct FilterGroup {
    pub field: String,
    pub values: Vec<FilterVal>,
}

/// Resolve the filter request into per-field groups of casted values.
/// Returns the groups actually usable (unknown field names are dropped);
/// an empty result means the original returns an empty list.
pub fn resolve_filters(resource: &str, params: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<FilterGroup> {
    let mut out: Vec<FilterGroup> = Vec::new();
    for (key, value) in params {
        if key.eq_ignore_ascii_case("output:only") {
            continue;
        }
        let ft = match filter_field_type(resource, key) {
            Some(ft) => ft,
            None => continue,
        };
        if filter_column(resource, key).is_none() {
            continue;
        }
        // canonical name
        let canon = restrictable_fields(resource)
            .iter()
            .find(|f| f.eq_ignore_ascii_case(key))
            .unwrap()
            .to_string();
        match out.iter_mut().find(|g| g.field == canon) {
            Some(existing) => existing.values.push(cast_filter_value(ft, value)),
            None => out.push(FilterGroup {
                field: canon,
                values: vec![cast_filter_value(ft, value)],
            }),
        }
    }
    out
}

pub async fn filter_ids(
    client: &tokio_postgres::Client,
    resource: &str,
    groups: &[FilterGroup],
) -> R<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut params: Vec<Box<dyn ToSql + Sync + Send>> = Vec::new();
    let mut wheres: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for g in groups {
        let col = filter_column(resource, &g.field).expect("checked column");
        let mut ors: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for v in &g.values {
            match v {
                FilterVal::None => {
                    // eq(field, null): never matches
                    ors.push("1 = 0".to_string());
                }
                FilterVal::Int(i) => {
                    let idx = params.len() + 1;
                    params.push(Box::new(*i));
                    ors.push(format!("{} = ${}", col, idx));
                }
                FilterVal::Str(s) => {
                    let idx = params.len() + 1;
                    params.push(Box::new(s.clone()));
                    ors.push(format!("{} = ${}", col, idx));
                }
                FilterVal::Bool(b) => {
                    let idx = params.len() + 1;
                    params.push(Box::new(*b));
                    ors.push(format!("{} = ${}", col, idx));
                }
                FilterVal::Double(f) => {
                    let idx = params.len() + 1;
                    params.push(Box::new(*f));
                    ors.push(format!("{} = ${}", col, idx));
                }
            }
        }
        if !ors.is_empty() {
            wheres.push(format!("({})", ors.join(" OR ")));
        }
    }
    let (base, root_alias) = match resource {
        "users" => (
            "SELECT p.id FROM persons p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.id",
            "p.id",
        ),
        "groups" => ("SELECT id FROM usergroups", "id"),
        "roles" => ("SELECT id FROM roles", "id"),
        "layers" => ("SELECT id FROM layers", "id"),
        "layerdatasources" => ("SELECT id FROM layerdatasources", "id"),
        "layerappearances" => ("SELECT id FROM layerappearances", "id"),
        _ => return Ok(Vec::new()),
    };
    let mut sql = String::from(base);
    if !wheres.is_empty() {
        sql.push_str(" WHERE ");
        sql.push_str(&wheres.join(" AND "));
    }
    sql.push_str(&format!(" ORDER BY {}", root_alias));
    let refs: Vec<&(dyn ToSql + Sync)> = params
        .iter()
        .map(|p| &**p as &(dyn ToSql + Sync))
        .collect();
    Ok(client.query(&sql, &refs).await?.iter().map(|r| r.get(0)).collect())
}

fn dedup_i32(v: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut out: Vec<i32> = Vec::new();
    for x in v {
        if !out.contains(x) {
            out.push(*x);
        }
    }
    out
}
